name: South Korea
note: Civil Act roles only. Korea has no grant of representation: inheritance commences by death and vests in the heir. The 2011 amendment (Act No. 10429) replaced incompetency declarations with a three-tier court guardianship — adult, limited and specific — plus a voluntary guardianship contract. Statutory text is the Korea Legislation Research Institute English translation; the Korean original governs.

citations.title: Definition of Mandate
citations.quote: A mandate shall become effective when one of the parties has entrusted the other party with the management of affairs and the other party has consented thereto.

citations.title: Death, Bankruptcy, etc. and Termination of Mandate
citations.quote: A mandate shall terminate upon the death or bankruptcy of either party. The same shall apply where the mandatory is adjudged to commence adult guardianship.

citations.title: Commencement of Guardianship by Adjudication on Commencement of Adult Guardianship
citations.quote: If an adjudication on the commencement of adult guardianship has been made by the Family Court, an adult guardian shall be appointed over such person who has been adjudicated as such.

citations.quote: An inheritance shall be commenced by death.

citations.title: Inheritance and Succession of Blanket Rights and Duties
citations.quote: An inheritor succeeds, from the time of the commencement of the inheritance, to the blanket rights and duties pertaining to the property of the inheritee: Provided , That this shall not apply to the property which is entirely personal to the inheritee.

citations.quote: A testator may designate an executor by will or commission a third person to designate an executor.

citations.title: Cases in which No Designated Executor Exists
citations.quote: If there exists no designated executor pursuant to the provisions of Articles 1093 and 1094 , an inheritor becomes an executor.

citations.quote: An executor has the right and duty to manage the property which is the subject of a testamentary gift, and to perform acts necessary for carrying out the will.

roles.name: Adult guardian
roles.summary: Appointed by the Family Court for a person who continuously lacks the capacity to manage affairs. The guardian is the ward’s legal representative, but the court sets how far that representation reaches and how far the guardian may decide personal affairs.

assigned.event: Family Court adjudicates commencement of adult guardianship on application by the principal, spouse, a relative within the fourth degree, a public prosecutor or the head of a local government

starts.event: An adult guardian is appointed once commencement is adjudged; the guardian becomes legal representative within the scope the court sets

ends.event: Family Court adjudicates termination once the cause for commencement has ceased
Death of the ward; the estate passes to the heirs by universal succession

states.label: Guardian acting as legal representative within court-set scope

transitions.event: Family Court adjudicates commencement of adult guardianship (art 9)
Adult guardian appointed; becomes legal representative, scope determined by the court (arts 929, 938)
Family Court modifies the scope of representation or of authority over personal affairs (art 938(4))
Cause for commencement ceases; Family Court adjudicates termination (art 11)
Death of the ward (arts 997, 1005)

roles.name: Limited guardian
roles.summary: A lighter court regime: the ward keeps capacity except for acts the court lists as needing the limited guardian’s consent. Representation is not automatic — the court must confer it separately.

assigned.event: Family Court adjudicates commencement of limited guardianship

starts.event: Court determines the scope of acts requiring the limited guardian’s consent; the court may separately confer a right of representation

ends.event: Guardianship contract supervisor appointed, or adult guardianship adjudged, displacing the limited guardianship

transitions.event: Family Court adjudicates commencement of limited guardianship (art 12)
Court determines or changes the acts needing the guardian’s consent (art 13)
Family Court adjudges to confer a right of representation (art 959-4)
Displaced by adult guardianship or by a voluntary guardianship supervisor (art 959-20)
Death of the ward (art 997)

roles.name: Specific guardian
roles.summary: Support for one matter or one period, and the only Korean guardianship that cannot be imposed over the principal’s objection. Representation is optional and time- and scope-limited when the court grants it.

assigned.event: Family Court adjudicates commencement of specific guardianship, fixing the period or the scope of affairs

starts.event: Court may confer a right of representation on the specific guardian for a set period and scope, and may require the supervisor’s consent to its exercise

ends.event: The fixed period expires or the specified affairs are completed

states.label: Support for set period or affairs
Representation conferred for set period and scope

transitions.event: Family Court adjudicates specific guardianship, fixing period or scope; it may not be exercised against the principal’s will (art 14-2)
Court confers a right of representation, setting period and scope (art 959-11)
Period expires or the specified affairs are completed (art 14-2(3))
Death of the principal (art 997)

roles.name: Voluntary guardian under a guardianship contract
roles.summary: Korea’s advance instrument. It must be made as an authentic deed and registered, and — unusually — it has no effect at all until the Family Court appoints a supervisor of voluntary guardianship, which it does once the principal is found to lack capacity.

assigned.event: Principal enters a guardianship contract in an authentic deed, entrusting property management and personal matters and conferring a right of representation

starts.event: Only when the Family Court appoints a supervisor of voluntary guardianship, the contract being registered and the principal deemed to lack capacity to manage affairs

ends.event: Contract terminates when commencement of adult or limited guardianship is adjudged for the principal

states.label: Contract in authentic deed, registered, not yet effective

transitions.event: Guardianship contract entered into in an authentic deed (art 959-14(1)-(2))
Family Court appoints a supervisor of voluntary guardianship; the contract takes effect at that time (arts 959-14(3), 959-15)
Adult or limited guardianship adjudged; the guardianship contract terminates (art 959-20(1))
Death of the principal (arts 997, 1005)

roles.name: Mandatary under an ordinary mandate
roles.summary: The ordinary agency relationship. It is not a durable instrument: it ends on the death or bankruptcy of either party, and also if the mandatary is placed under adult guardianship.

assigned.event: Mandate entrusts the mandatary with the management of affairs, and the mandatary accepts

ends.event: Death or bankruptcy of either party, or the mandatary is adjudged to commence adult guardianship

transitions.event: Mandate entrusted and accepted (art 680)
Death or bankruptcy of either party, or adult guardianship adjudged for the mandatary (art 690)

roles.name: Heir
roles.summary: Korea has no grant of representation: inheritance commences by death and the heir succeeds to the blanket rights and duties of the estate from that moment. The heir has three months from learning of the commencement to accept absolutely, accept with limitation, or renounce.

starts.event: The heir succeeds to the blanket rights and duties of the estate from the time inheritance commences, with no grant

ends.event: Renunciation within three months of learning of the commencement, or the period passes with absolute acceptance

states.label: Estate vested in heir on death

transitions.event: Death commences the inheritance; blanket rights and duties pass to the heir (arts 997, 1005)
Acceptance, absolute or qualified, within three months of learning of the commencement (art 1019)
Renunciation within the same three-month period, extendable by the Family Court (art 1019)

roles.name: Executor of a will
roles.summary: Designated in the will, or by a third person the testator commissions. Where nobody is designated, the heir is the executor by operation of law. The executor manages the property given by will and does what is needed to carry it out.

assigned.event: Testator designates an executor by will, or commissions a third person to designate one

starts.event: On the testator’s death the executor holds the right and duty to manage the bequeathed property and to perform the acts necessary to carry out the will

ends.event: The acts necessary to carry out the will are performed

transitions.event: Testator designates an executor by will, or commissions a third person to do so (art 1093)
No executor designated, so the heir becomes executor (art 1095)
Death of the testator; executor manages the bequeathed property (arts 997, 1101)
Acts necessary to carry out the will are performed (art 1101)

roles.name: Administrator of an estate with no known heir
roles.summary: Where it is unknown whether an heir exists, the court appoints an administrator of the inherited property on the application of a relative or other interested party.

assigned.event: Court appoints an administrator on application, where it is unknown whether an heir exists

ends.event: An heir is found and accepts, or the administration is completed

transitions.event: Court appoints an administrator where it is unknown whether an heir exists (art 1053)
Heir found, or administration completed (art 1053)

poaDurableByDefault.note: An ordinary mandate ends on the death or bankruptcy of either party; the durable instrument is the guardianship contract, which needs an authentic deed and takes effect only when the Family Court appoints a supervisor.

springingPoaAllowed.note: The guardianship contract is inherently springing: it takes effect at the time the Family Court appoints a supervisor of voluntary guardianship, once the principal is deemed to lack capacity to manage affairs.

poaRegistrationBeforeUse.note: The contract must be registered, and a supervisor appointed by the Family Court, before it has effect.

supportedDecisionMakingStatute.name: Specific guardianship, Civil Act arts 14-2 and 959-11 (added by Act No. 10429, 7 Mar 2011)

probateGrantName.note: No grant of representation. Inheritance is commenced by death and the heir succeeds to the blanket rights and duties of the estate from that moment.
